intro: We help UK residents apply for all four Ghana visa options: the tourist visa, business visa, e-Tourist visa and e-Business visa. Choose the visa that matches your trip below. We prepare your application and check your documents, including your yellow fever certificate.

faqs.q: How long does a Ghana visa take?
faqs.a: It depends on the option. eVisas are often decided within a few working days, while High Commission visas can take several weeks, and longer around Christmas and festival periods. Express options may be available.

faqs.q: Should I get a Ghana visa or a Ghana eVisa?
faqs.a: Both are valid for tourism and business trips. The eVisa is applied for online, so you keep your passport and decisions are often faster. The High Commission visa can suit travellers who prefer a visa in their passport or whose case doesn't fit the eVisa. We'll tell you which is best for your trip.

faqs.q: Do British citizens need a Ghana visa?
faqs.a: Yes. British citizens need a visa to visit Ghana, applied for before travel.

faqs.q: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for a Ghana visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Ghana requires a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate for entry, and visa applications usually ask for it.

sections.heading: Do you need a visa for Ghana?
sections.text: British citizens need a visa to visit Ghana. You can apply through the Ghana High Commission in London or online with an eVisa. Processing times vary, so apply well before you travel.

sections.heading: Ghana visa options
sections.text:
There are four ways to get a Ghana visa from the UK. We can help with all of them:
- Tourist visa: for holidays and visiting family or friends, applied for through the Ghana High Commission in London
- Business visa: for meetings, conferences and business trips, applied for through the Ghana High Commission in London
- e-Tourist visa: the online version of the tourist visa, with no need to send your passport away
- e-Business visa: the online version of the business visa, for meetings and business trips

Ghana launched its eVisa system in May 2026. The eVisa is often quicker, but the High Commission route is still available and can suit some travellers better. If you're not sure which to choose, we'll advise you.

sections.heading: What you will usually need
sections.text:
Most Ghana visa applications need:
- Your passport, valid for at least 6 months, with blank pages
- A completed application form and passport photos
- A return flight booking
- Hotel bookings, or an invitation letter from your host in Ghana with a copy of their ID
- For business trips, a letter from your employer and an invitation from the Ghanaian company
- A yellow fever vaccination certificate

sections.heading: Yellow fever certificate
sections.text: Ghana requires all arriving travellers to show a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate. Get vaccinated at least 10 days before you travel, at a registered yellow fever centre.

sections.heading: Ghana visa help in Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and help travellers and businesses across the North West and the rest of the UK. Most travel visa applications can be handled by post and email, so you don't need to visit us in person.
